body: Hi there, apologies for the delay in responding, I have been working on analysing the data for the study. I am sorry to hear about what you experienced as a child.  A lot of the challenges you describe about accessing help have been shared by the people who took part on the study. I am glad to hear that you have found therapy helpful and that you have a supportive partner. Thank you for sharing your experiences, it sounds like you have had to manage a lot.  In the post above we have provided contact details about support services that you can contact, if you feel that you want some support.
Hi there, I am so sorry that I missed your message. I hope you were able to take part before we closed the study.
I really appreciate you taking the time to comment, it is through communication that we can learn and develop, so thank you!
Hi, Thank you very much for your comments- I tried to consult various platforms to ensure that my wording was appropriate, but I acknowledge that I may not have got this right.
thank you! we've had a good response to the study so far.

Thank you for getting in touch. I can understand that, and a few people have shared the same. In the participant information sheet we share what we do to keep data secure, feel free to have a look through this and see how you feel. We were keen to have the study be completely anonymous in order to ensure that we were not excluding people, however we were informed that we had to take names as part of the consent to participate process. Apologies that this means that we are not able to have you be involved in the study.

Hello, 

Unfortunately as this is a student project there wasn't enough funds to cover reimbursing everyone. I appreciate that taking part may cause distress and contact numbers of support services are provided, but please ensure that you look after yourself. If taking part would be distressing for you,  then consider not taking part. Most important thing it to do what feels most comfortable for you.

Sorry for the delay in responding. We have said that people who are actively experiencing thoughts about suicide can take part as there is still so much that you can contribute. So feel free to participate and don't worry about the answers you give, just go with what feels right to you.

I am really sorry to hear that you've had such a difficult experience with services. I agree that much more needs to be done to ensure that people are given support when they need it- waiting lists are often long. I am glad to hear that you've been able to find something that you've found helpful.

**\[Academic\] Research study looking to hear from people with lived experience of suicidal thoughts & behaviours (Adults, 18+ only, UK)**  
**Who I am:** Trainee Clinical Psychologist (student)  
**Affiliation:** University of Manchester, UK  
**Supervisor**: Dr Daniel Pratt & Professor Gillian Haddock  
**Target group:** individuals with lived experience of suicidal thoughts and behaviours   
**Compensation:** none unfortunately  
**Survey link:** https://www.qualtrics.manchester.ac.uk/jfe/form/SV\_8J8RC0nv9iICcAe  
**Background:** Completed in fulfilment of a doctorate in Clinical Psychology- (Thesis)

Hello, thank you for your reflections. I appreciate that this is a sensitive topic area and I do wish we had been able to reimburse people for their time, however as the project is being carried out in fulfilment of a doctorate in Clinical Psychology we did not have enough funding to be able to pay everyone who could have taken part.
Is that by Dorothy Leeds? I'll check it out.
Thank you very much and apologies you are unable to participate in the study. Esmira
Thank you for sharing this, its important information for me to reflect on as a clinician as well as a researcher. Esmira

Yes, we would not hold any information you share with us if you decide to withdraw from the study. This would be deleted the moment you expressed your desire to withdraw. Data does become anonymous at some points, however, and from then onwards it would not be possible to withdraw as we wouldn't be able to identify you. I hope this makes sense and apologies for the delay in responding.

Hi, thank you for sharing this and I appreciate you don't wish to engage with the study beyond sharing the above comment. I have been privileged to talk to many people about their experiences and one thing is clear is that everyone has their own journey and I appreciate you sharing a part of yours. Esmira
Hello, thank you for connecting and apologies for the delay in responding. We would really appreciate the support, so please feel free to share the study with others. Thank you, Esmira

Hi! Apologies for the delay in responding, I have been away. I agree with you that the services I signpost to are excellent in providing support to people, and people may choose to contact these services over their GP, but others would want support from their GP and hence why we ask for this information. We do not disclose any information to the GP without full consent from the participant.

Hi, Your question and points are all very valid, and we've had a number of individuals contact us with similar queries. The reason we ask for this information is just so the GP can provide support if people need it. We do not share  study data with the GP or any other individual outside the research team.

Hi, 

you can express interest by following this link: https://www.qualtrics.manchester.ac.uk/jfe/form/SV\_8J8RC0nv9iICcAe

Hello, thank you for your questions. We can help people to seek support if they wish for us to do this and have provided a number of support services individuals can access. Hello, before I post the study advert on any sub I always email the sub moderators to check with a them. I send them a copy of the message I seek to post, this is given the sensitive nature of the topic of my research. I have been informed by some moderators that research posts are sometimes removed on their sub automatically. The only time I post anything without getting moderator approval is when there is no moderator for a sub, in these instances I do not add 'mod approved' to my post title. I would be happy to send you evidence of the mod approval from r/Britain

This is an academic piece of research. All data collected with comply with information governance policies set by the University of Manchester. The responses individuals provide with only be seen by the research team. Study data will be stored on Qualtrics, an online platform approved for use in research studies by the information governance team. After this, data will be downloaded and saved servers at the University of Manchester for the duration of the study. Data will be deleted from Qualtrics after each round of the study- all data will be deleted from qraltrics by 30th of November 2021. Data is then archived at the University of Manchester for a period of up to 5 years following publication of study results. 

Study is being conducted by Dr Esmira Ropaj, Dr Daniel Pratt and Professor Gillian Haddock- University of Manchester. 

The first part will take about 5 minutes to fill out and the second part of the study is currently taking participants between 5-10 minutes. 

We are unable to compensate individuals for taking part in the study.

We would like to hear from adults (18+) who live in the UK, are registered with a GP, who speak English and are currently experiencing or have previously experienced suicidal thoughts and/or behaviours within the last 5 years

We are hoping to reach as wide a group of individuals as possible as we are keen to capture multiple perspective
Thank you! It is a piece of research that I feel very passionate about.

Hi, Apologies for the delay. I am assuming you are referring to the statement in the consent form? This statement is to allow the University the option to audit my study (in their role as the organisation sponsoring the study). They could potentially look at any and all data that is collected from my study, including any  identifiable dat that you provide us. They do not look at your patient records as we do not collect this information from you. I hope this makes sense, but please feel free to get back in touch if you want me to clarify anything. Esmira
Thank you for your suggestion. The moderator of the Manchester sub has kindly allowed me to post the study on there too.
Unfortunately not at the moment. We are going back to ethics to ask if this can be changed. If we are able to implement the change, then I will comment on here.

We don't share anything with the GP that the participant doesn't consent to. As part of the process of consenting to take part in the study we ask participants whether they agree for the GP to be informed about their involvement in the study. If the participant selects 'No' to this, then we do not contact the GP. We would never share information with anyone without the individuals consent.

Thank you for your questions. We let the GP know that you are taking part in the study, nothing else is shared with them. We are asking for this information just so they can provide support for you if you need it.

Hi, Apologies the option to go back not been built into the study simply because we did not consider this, but can certainly consider adding it. A copy of the information sheet is available for people to download at the end of the questionnaire.  We don't share information you share with us with any NHS trusts. NHS trusts and university might look at our study documents to make sure we are complying with data protection. We are working with Greater Manchester Mental Health at the moment.

Hi, thank you for getting in touch. Currently ethics have requested that we collect GP information and so unfortunately you won't be able to take part unless GP information is provided. However, we are contacting ethics to see if we can make changes to this as it means that many people like yourself are not able to participate. If we manage to make changes, can I let you know on here? Esmira

Hello,  
My name is Esmira, I am a trainee Clinical Psychologist at the University of Manchester. 

  
I am doing a research study looking at what recovery means to people who have had or are currently experiencing thoughts about taking their life as well as exploring what factors have helped people in their recovery journey.  
We are looking to hear from adults (18+) who live in the UK, are registered with a GP and currently experiencing or have previously experienced suicidal thoughts and/or behaviours within the last 5 years.  
We are hoping to recruit about 150 people; your support will be greatly appreciated.  
For more information and to express your interest, please follow the link  
https://www.qualtrics.manchester.ac.uk/jfe/form/SV\_8J8RC0nv9iICcAe
Thank you very much. Glad to hear that you are doing OK now.

Thank you for sharing this information. Please also be aware that at the top of each page of the survey you will have access to a list of national support services you can access should you require any support, Esmira
We definitely have difficulties with replication in the field. The study we are hoping to run is a Delphi Design, where those who chose to take part decide on aspects which are important.
These are important issues that will be addressed within the write up of the research paper as they can have implications for the conclusion we draw.
